notes: Fixed string ends and closed pipe ends are displacement nodes; an open pipe end is a displacement antinode. Adjacent nodes are λ/2 apart; a node and adjacent antinode are λ/4 apart.
Two like ends allow L = nλ/2. One open and one closed end allows L = (2n − 1)λ/4. Use the mode shown, not automatically the fundamental.

sup-7b98eef406c31dfd-w4:c.i.hint: Find the effective stiffness that acts on the oscillating mass about its equilibrium position.
notes: For a mass on an ideal spring, T = 2π√(m/k). Adding springs or masses can change the effective k or m.
A constant gravitational force shifts the equilibrium of a vertical spring but does not change this ideal period. Keep extension from natural length separate from displacement about equilibrium.
For “show that”, start from the supplied data and display the intermediate steps. Do not substitute the result you are asked to show as an assumption.

sup-7b98eef406c31dfd-w4:c.ii.hint: Find the effective stiffness that acts on the oscillating mass about its equilibrium position.
notes: For a mass on an ideal spring, T = 2π√(m/k). Adding springs or masses can change the effective k or m.
A constant gravitational force shifts the equilibrium of a vertical spring but does not change this ideal period. Keep extension from natural length separate from displacement about equilibrium.

sup-7b98eef406c31dfd-w4:c.iii.hint: First decide whether the source and observer are getting closer or farther apart.
notes: For sound, source motion changes the spacing of wavefronts; observer motion changes how quickly they are encountered. Choose the Doppler signs so approach increases observed frequency.
For collinear motion, f_obs = f_source(v ± v_observer)/(v ∓ v_source), with speeds measured relative to the medium. Do not simply exchange source and observer speeds.
Use any result supplied above directly where needed. You do not need to redo an earlier calculation from another topic.

sup-7b98eef406c31dfd-w4:d.i.hint: Compare oscillation energy at the start and end of the stated interval.
notes: With unchanged mass and natural frequency, total oscillator energy is proportional to amplitude squared. Read the envelope amplitudes at the two times.
Average power lost is (E_initial − E_final)/Δt. A halved amplitude does not mean only half the energy is lost.
For the sketch, label both axes and show the correct intercepts, turning points and limiting behaviour. A qualitative sketch still needs the correct physical trend.

sup-7b98eef406c31dfd-w4:d.ii.hint: Check whether the wave is observed directly or after reflection from a moving object.
notes: Beat frequency is the absolute difference between two received frequencies. Determine the Doppler-shifted frequency before subtracting.
A moving reflector can produce two Doppler shifts, once when receiving and once when reradiating. Do not treat an echo automatically as a single moving-source problem.
Link the relevant physical cause to the observation asked about. Naming a law alone does not explain why this particular result follows.
